title: LossDomain
description: The loss a content type must survive: losing one device, one household, or one region. An app manifest declares it per content type (`needs.loss`, a demand rule, not a need); the space's charter resolves it to holders and failure domains (`Charter::resolve`, never below the charter's holding floor), so joining a space with a stricter charter changes placement without changing the app (interfaces spec §D.7, §G worked example). Ordered from the narrowest loss to the widest; it is not a reach and carries no `_ordinal`. Source of truth: this schema; Rust mirror `placement_core::LossDomain` (decide.rs). TypeScript constants only: `_codegen` (no `rust` key, so codegen-rs writes nothing) and never `_dna`, so no constant reaches content_store_integrity and no DNA hash moves (interfaces spec §2.G, G11). placement-core's schema_contract test reads this file with include_str! and compares it, in order, with the variants of `placement_core::LossDomain` written out by hand inside that test. It catches a value changed here, but a variant added to the Rust enum without editing the test still passes: nothing ties the test's list to the enum (follow-on: an `ALL` const in decide.rs held to the enum by an exhaustive match, read by the test).
